step_by_step_reasoning:
1. Identify external actors from whiteboard: 'STUDENTS' (UserConsumerWeb) and 'AUTHORS' (UserCompanyDeveloper).
2. Identify AWS services drawn as distinct nodes: ELB, S3, RedShift, two EKS clusters (Inference and Training), SageMaker, ECR, CloudWatch.
3. Identify visual data flows based strictly on drawn arrows:
   - Students event data to S3.
   - Authors event data to RedShift.
   - S3 data transformed/loaded into RedShift.
   - RedShift to EKS (Training) for model building.
   - EKS (Training) to SageMaker for hyperparameter tuning.
   - SageMaker outputting docker image to ECR.
   - ECR deploying model to top EKS (Inference).
   - Students accessing the system via ELB, which routes to top EKS (Inference).
4. CloudWatch is visually present on the whiteboard without direct physical arrows attached, so it is kept as an isolated node following visual-first principles.
